answer: One concrete defense is earned standing backed by a small slashable bond. A newcomer starts like a sparrow at the edge of the flock: it may take tiny, low-value jobs, but it cannot vote or move large funds until independent peers have attested a history of useful work. To graduate, it posts a copper-denominated bond that is slashed for fraud, and its reputation acts as a lantern — visible to everyone, hard to fake, and slow to rebuild — so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs far more than it can ever earn.
